source_text: In his ergo ab exilio suo perducebantur ad praesidem Agapius et Secundinus episcopi praedicandi, ambo spiritali dilectione concordes, alter et carnalis continentiae sanctitate. Perducebantur, inquam, non a poena, sicut gentilibus uidebatur, ad poenam, sed a gloria potius ad gloriam, a certamine ad certamen aliud, ut qui captiosas saeculi pompas in obtinendo Christi nomine subegissent, etiam mortis aculeos consummatae fidei uirtute calcarent. Neque enim fas erat ut tardius quaererent in terrena conluctatione uictoriam, quos iam dominus secum habere properabat. Et contigit, fratres, ut Agapius et Secundinus ex inlustri sacerdotio martyres gloriosi, in eo transitu quo ad beatae passionis suae praelium, praesidis quidem temporali potestate, sed Christi electione pergebant, nostrum intrare dignarentur hospitium. Quibus tantus inerat spiritus uiuificationis et gratiae, ut tam sanctis et tam praeclaris dei testibus iam parum esset quod ipsi martyrio glorioso pretiosum sanguinem destinassent, nisi etiam alios martyras fidei suae inspiratione fecissent. Horum tanta in fratres caritas fuit et tanta dilectio, ut licet taciti possent tam deuotae et obstinatae uirtutis exemplis fidem fraternitatis adstruere, tamen ad stabilitatem perseuerantiae latius consulentes, pectoribus nostris rorem tractatus salutaris infunderent; neque enim tacere poterant qui dei sermone uiuebant. Nec mirum si paucis illis diebus tam large nostrum omnium mentes eorum tractatus salubris animauit, in quibus iam Christus micante gratia de proxima passione fulgebat.
thought_title: Exiled bishops led to death encourage their hosts
orientation: The narrator tells how Agapius and Secundinus are being brought from exile to the governor and enter the home where Marian and James are staying.
pass_a_gloss: Among these therefore from their own exile were being led to the governor Agapius and Secundinus, bishops to be proclaimed, both united by spiritual love, the one also by holiness of bodily continence. They were being led, I say, not from punishment, as it seemed to the pagans, to punishment, but rather from glory to glory, from struggle to another struggle, so that they who had subdued the ensnaring pomps of the world in obtaining the name of Christ, might also trample the stings of death by the strength of completed faith. For it was not right that they should seek victory in earthly wrestling too slowly, whom the Lord was already hastening to have with himself. And it happened, brothers, that Agapius and Secundinus, glorious martyrs from illustrious priesthood, on that passage by which they were going to the battle of their blessed suffering, by the temporal power of the governor indeed, but by the choice of Christ, deigned to enter our lodging. In them so great a spirit of life-giving and of grace was present, that for such holy and such distinguished witnesses of God it was now too little that they themselves had destined their precious blood for glorious martyrdom, unless they also made other martyrs by the inspiration of their faith. Such great love toward the brothers was theirs and such great affection, that although silent they could have built up the faith of the brotherhood by the examples of such devoted and obstinate courage, nevertheless consulting more widely for the firmness of perseverance, they poured into our breasts the dew of salutary discourse; for they could not be silent who were living by the word of God. Nor is it surprising if in those few days their wholesome discourse so abundantly enlivened the minds of all of us, in whom Christ was already shining with glittering grace from the approaching suffering.

choices.why: Gerundive agreeing with bishops; keeps proclaiming sense and avoids adding illustrious.
Brief fixes bishops as models; sacerdotium is office, not yet martyrs.
Literal for testibus here; not yet using glossary martyrs because source does not write martyribus.
Keeps metaphor rorem and medical sense salutaris; tractatus is spoken teaching.
Literal wrestling image matching certamen and praelium nearby.

pass_b_english: At this point Agapius and Secundinus were led from their own exile to the governor as bishops to be proclaimed. The two were united in spiritual love, and one was marked also by holy continence of the flesh. They were led, I say, not from punishment to punishment, as it looked to pagans, but from glory to glory, from one struggle to another. For they had subdued the ensnaring show of the world in winning Christ's name, so they might also trample the stings of death by the power of a perfected faith. Nor was it right for them to seek victory in earthly wrestling too slowly, when the Lord was already hastening to have them with himself.

And it happened, brothers, that Agapius and Secundinus, glorious martyrs from illustrious priesthood, deigned to enter our lodging while they were passing toward the battle of their blessed passion. They went by the governor's temporal power, yet by Christ's choice. So great a spirit of life-giving and grace dwelt in them that, holy and renowned as these witnesses of God were, it was no longer enough for them to have destined their precious blood for glorious martyrdom. They also made other martyrs by the inspiration of their faith.

So great was their love and affection for the brothers that, although in silence they could have built up the faith of the brotherhood by the example of such devoted and unyielding courage, they looked more widely to the firmness of our endurance and poured into our hearts the dew of salutary discourse. For those who lived by God's word could not keep silent. Nor is it surprising that in those few days their salutary discourse so richly enlivened all our minds, for in them Christ was already shining with flashing grace from their approaching passion.
notes: Source keeps inlustri for illustri and martyras for martyres; glossed as written.
alter et carnalis continentiae sanctitate is compressed; glossed as one also distinguished by holiness of bodily continence without inventing which man.
